notes: Identity assessment: supplied text identifies the University of Birmingham peer reviewed version of A Psychological Intervention Reduces Doping Likelihood in British and Greek Athletes: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial; title-page authors match Kavussanu, Barkoukis, Hurst, Yukhymenko-Lescroart, Skoufa, Chirico, Lucidi, and Ring; cover DOI is 10.1016/j.psychsport.2021.102099 and published citation is Psychology of Sport and Exercise 61, 102099 (2022). This is a primary accepted report, not a secondary account. The cache explicitly consists of selected overlapping PDF-page windows, not a complete transcription. No PDF path supplied; no PDF rendering or acquisition performed. P markers are zero-based and include a university cover. The description names no outcome, time contrast, intervention contrast, or analysis population; p. 18 includes moral disengagement, anticipated guilt and self-regulatory efficacy and several simple/total/interaction effects. Page numbering also differs from physical PDF indexing. No unique target can be selected from study 1 and the broad description. Candidate model samples only: Table 4 reports ITT N = 208 athletes and PP N = 141 athletes; Table 5 reports corresponding k = 19 and k = 18 clubs. Athletes and clubs are distinct units; no N is derived from df or summed. ITT uses all available data; PP requires all six sessions and all waves (listwise deletion). These are model-scope candidates, not a verified row-specific analytic N because neither outcome/test nor ITT versus PP is identified. Printed p. 18 contains secondary outcomes, not a unique test. Moral disengagement candidates: pre-post educational/reference slope ∆M = -.39, ES = -.38; total psychological change ∆M = -.54, ES = -.52; total educational change ∆M = -.44, ES = -.42; total between-intervention difference ∆M = -.10, ES = -.10. Anticipated guilt total changes: psychological ∆M = 1.83, ES = .95; educational ∆M = .76, ES = .40; between-intervention difference ∆M = 1.06, ES = .55. Self-regulatory efficacy pre-post simple slopes: psychological ∆M = -.35, ES = -.21; educational ∆M = .40, ES = .23. Adjacent p. 17 primary-outcome doping-likelihood candidates include psychological pre-post ES = -.44, educational post-follow-up ES = -.27, total psychological ES = -.54, total educational ES = -.41, and total between-intervention ES = -.13. The printed ES metric is baseline standard deviation units (p. 16 and table notes), not explicitly named Cohen d; do not relabel or convert. The inspected results and Tables 4-5 give estimates, SEs, 95% CIs and ES, and significance is explicitly evaluated using whether CIs contain zero. They do not print target-specific p values in these sections. No p is reconstructed from CIs or SEs, and no whole-work absence is claimed for this partial cached text.
